newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras moved toward normal ties with Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Honduras moved toward normal ties with Cuba.

text.p: Honduras said on Wednesday it was taking a first step toward re-establishing normal diplomatic relations with Cuba.
Honduras broke off diplomatic ties in 1961, but the two countries on Wednesday formally swapped "interest sections" in each other's capitals to function in lieu of an embassy or consulate.

"This can be considered a fist step ... toward establishing full diplomatic relations," Roberto Arita, the Honduran deputy foreign minister, told reporters. He declined to predict when full relations might be expected, noting that Cuba had had an informal office in Honduras since 1990.

In 1961, Honduras followed the lead of the United States in attempting to isolate Cuba two years after Castro came to power in a revolution. Castro remains in command of the one-party, Communist state.
